newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng hits new record closing high.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng hits new record closing high.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng index recorded its third record closing high in under a week on Tuesday, driven higher by continued interest in property and banking stocks, brokers said.
The Hang Seng index closed the session at a record 12,490.70, up 160.35 points. Turnover was HK$8.41 billion.
The blue chip index began its record breaking move last Wednesday and also scored a record closing high on Monday.

"People are enjoying a bit of euphoria at the moment because U.S. interest rates did not go up," said Keith Irving, head of research at HG Asia. "The rally does still seem to really be led in the main by four or five big stocks," he said.
Among Tuesday's big gainers were HSBC Holdings, up HK$2.00 at HK$151.50, Hang Seng Bank, up HK$2.50 at HK$92.75, Cheung Kong, up HK$1.50 at HK$62.50, and Henderson Land, up HK$1.00 at HK$70.50.
"The concentration is still on the big blue chip companies - the major banks and some of the property developers," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.

"These are companies that have posted continuous growth. After first-half earnings, most of us revised our profit forecasts upwards and because of these upward revisions analysts have been issuing buy recommendations," he said.

Analysts said record highs scored on Wall Street on Monday had given sentiment in the local market a boost. The Dow Industrials rose 40.62 points to close above 6,000 points for the first time ever at 6,010.00.
"If you look at the volume and the focus, then you would say the market probably still has about 600 to 700 points to go from this level," said Tang of the Hang Seng.

Analysts said the market was looking overbought but the momentum was strong. "I think a lot of people have been saying that it will come to an end but it has continued to go up. We might see some gains over the next couple of days," said Irving.
Swire Pacific closed HK$1.00 higher at HK$71.75, CITIC Pacific jumped HK$0.90 to HK$38.30 and Wheelock gained HK$0.65 to HK$17.85. The H-share index rallied 9.97 points to 862.41.
